findings.title: When several countries share a dialing code, the prefix match overrides the user's own region.
findings.body:
`defaultPhoneCountry` prefers `findCountryByPhonePrefix` over `fallbackCountry`. Several countries can share the same prefix digits: Canada and the US (and possibly NANP territories) all use `+1`, and Russia and Kazakhstan both use `+7`. In that case `find` returns whichever comes first in the `countries` list. So a user in Canada with a prefilled `+1...` number sees the flag of whichever `+1` country is listed first, often the US, even though their own region matches the number. The same thing happens to a user in Kazakhstan with a `+7` number.

Fix: if `fallbackCountry`'s prefix digits match the start of `initialNumber`, keep `fallbackCountry`. Only fall back to `findCountryByPhonePrefix` when the user's region does not match the number.
